fact_text: Shaukat Hussain started in 2018 by selling fish online from his father's fish shop, and noticed strong demand for Pangasius from restaurants and caterers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Samak Farm began biofloc fish farming with five 10,000-litre tanks on a plot on the Northern Bypass.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Samak Farm now runs about 18 of its own tanks for production, seed and probiotics work.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Samak Farm provides one-window services to farmers: project design, fish seed, probiotics and feed, plus help selling the harvest. It has over 100 service customers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Making its own probiotics cut the cost to about Rs 2.5 per ml, against about Rs 170 per ml when imported from Thailand, according to the founder.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Stocking 1,000 fish seed in one 20-foot biofloc tank costs about Rs 8,000.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Total cost per 20-foot biofloc tank, including seed, probiotics and labour, can reach about Rs 120,000 over a nine-month crop cycle.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Feed is a major operating cost over the nine-month cycle; the founder wants local feed mills to bring feed costs down.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: A 20-foot biofloc tank yields about 650-750 kg of fish per crop, and the founder said almost all of it is saleable production.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder stocks one fish per 90 litres of water to reach a target of about 1.5 kg per fish at harvest.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder cited a 20-foot tank holding about 35,000 litres of water as an example, noting that fish growth depends on water volume rather than tank size.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said fish are priced by size: a 1.5 kg fish sells for about Rs 750-800, while smaller fish fetch much less per kilogram.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said buyers in restaurants, caterers and marts want large fish, and that large fish also yield bigger, better boneless fillets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: In biofloc farming, bacteria convert fish waste into floc that fish eat, while overstocking produces ammonia that kills fish if water is not controlled.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said the alternative to biofloc, repeated full water changes, is costly where electricity is expensive and solar power only runs in daytime.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said Pangasius imports into Pakistan fell about 90% once local biofloc production grew, from 30-40 containers a month previously.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Before local biofloc production grew, about 30 to 40 containers of Pangasius were imported into Pakistan each month, according to the founder.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: A Saudi importer asked Samak Farm for 10 tonnes of fish a week, but its small tanks produce only about 5-6 tonnes a year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: A container holds about 25 tonnes of fish, and the founder's stated goal is to supply at least one container a month from local production.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Samak Farm stocks about 500 fish per acre and set a target of at least 1,500 kg of production per acre, up from about 500 kg per acre at the earlier stage.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: Samak Farm set up a 140-acre trial in Thatta comparing traditional farming with biofloc farming, and reported that production was doubled or tripled in the new system.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said one biofloc tank adds a power load of about 100 watts, so a single bore and a modest supply can run a farm.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said more than 30 species can be farmed in the setup; Pangasius is advised for Karachi, while rohu, gulfam and murakhi are advised for interior Sindh.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said Samak Farm's fish is fully organic with no chemical treatment, unlike Vietnamese fillets, which are chemically processed to look white.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said Samak Farm's fish is sold as brand-packed product, as fillets, and to restaurants and catering businesses.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder argued farming is intensifying as land shrinks, citing poultry farms that moved from about one shed per acre to 8,000-16,000 birds per acre.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said biofloc uses less water and less space than pond farming and produces more per unit, calling it the way forward for the sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: The founder said many cattle farmers suffered losses in 2025 because they had to buy water for animals and import fodder.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)

fact_text: A Karachi fish farmer who had trained in Thailand reportedly spent about Rs 2 million on training and refused to teach the founder for Rs 50,000, keeping the technique as a monopoly.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Selling Fish to Owning Biofloc Farms: Shaukat Hussain's Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-04-10)
